lines.text: Financial services encompass a vast industry that manages, invests, and protects money. Insurance is a contract where a company agrees to compensate for specific losses in exchange for regular premium payments. Types include life insurance (pays out on death), health insurance (covers medical costs), home insurance (property and contents), motor insurance (vehicle cover), and travel insurance. Investment services help individuals and companies grow their wealth through stocks (shares in companies), bonds (loans to governments or corporations), mutual funds (pooled investments managed professionally), and pensions (long-term retirement savings). Financial advisors help clients plan for major life events: buying a home, funding education, planning retirement, and managing inheritance. Tax planning involves understanding income tax, capital gains tax, VAT (Value Added Tax), and tax relief on pensions and charitable donations. Fintech — financial technology — has disrupted traditional banking with digital-only banks, peer-to-peer lending, cryptocurrency, robo-advisors, and budgeting apps. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) regulates UK financial services, ensuring consumer protection and market integrity. Key consumer protections include the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), which guarantees deposits up to £85,000 per institution. Understanding financial services vocabulary empowers people to make informed decisions, avoid scams, and build long-term financial security.
